name: Storm manta

baseline.name: Storm manta
baseline.look: Wide amber-gray glider with fin ribbons and luminous throat spots.
baseline.ecology: Feeds on airborne spores and follows predictable pressure fronts.
baseline.limit: Wing turbulence threatens light craft; it cannot summon a storm.
baseline.encounter: Sail crews read ribbon position and give the feeding column space.
baseline.scale_note: Adult representative staging envelope; individuals vary by up to 10%. Not shown at common scale on the art plate.

daily: A manta glides along pressure fronts through airborne spore columns. Its fin ribbons stream differently before a turn. Luminous throat spots remain anatomical features rather than warning lights for travelers.
cycle: Seasonal spore blooms draw loose feeding groups. Weather moves the column; the creatures follow it. They cannot create a storm to arrive on cue.
signs: Ribbons draw inward before a banking turn; pale spore haze becomes visible against darker clouds. Clear blue sky does not guarantee an empty flight lane.
escalation: Glide -> bank -> feed through column -> turbulence wake. Collision is the danger. A crew cannot negotiate with the animal or count on it avoiding a sail.
community: Aurel Quay dispatchers publish observed feeding lanes alongside weather and loading limits. Delay means feeding passengers and paying stranded crews, not simply declaring safety virtuous.
scene: Eri rejects a clear-looking launch lane. A rival claims she is protecting her own business; she shares observations and opens the record to another crew’s correction.
motion: A broad rigid wing root supports flexible tips. Animate one banking action with a coherent body axis; ribbons lag the turn. No constant full-body wobble.
sounds: Wind shear and sail buffeting; throat resonance is animal sound, never a storm-summoning song.
rule: 22 m span, 12 m length. Weather-bound glider, not a magic flying vehicle.
canon_status: Additive ecology and production guidance; proposed scene remains unadopted.
